# Data {#sec-data}

```{python}
exec(open("_common.py").read())
g = games()
lines = pd.read_parquet(RAW / "lines.parquet")
adv = pd.read_parquet(RAW / "advanced.parquet")
```

## Sources

| Need | Source | Access |
|---|---|---|
| Games, venue, neutral site, conference game, final score | ESPN scoreboard (`groups=80`, FBS) | Free, no key |
| **Points by quarter** (Q1–Q4, OT) | ESPN scoreboard `linescores` | Free, no key |
| Betting lines: spread, total, moneyline, open and close | CollegeFootballData `/lines` [@cfbd] | Free key, 3,000 calls/month |
| Efficiency per team-game: plays, EPA/PPA, success rate, explosiveness, pass/rush splits | CFBD `/stats/game/advanced` | Same key |
| Talent composite, returning production | CFBD `/talent`, `/player/returning` | Same key |

: Data sources. {#tbl-sources}

CFBD game ids are the same as ESPN's, so every table joins on `game_id`. Tables keyed by
school name (advanced stats, talent, returning production) map to ids through **FBS
teams only**, because some names repeat across divisions (there's more than one
"Charlotte" and "Troy").

## Ingestion and caching

Both clients (`src/canes_cfb/espn.py`, `cfbd.py`) cache every raw response as JSON under
`data/raw/`:

- **ESPN:** a week whose games are all final is never downloaded again. Weeks with
  unfinished games are refreshed.
- **CFBD:** one call per season per endpoint. Past seasons are never requested twice,
  and the current season is refreshed. A full rebuild of 2015–2026 costs ~60 calls.

The data itself is **never committed** (`data/` is git-ignored, ~220 MB). It can be
rebuilt from the notebooks in `00_data/`, and republishing ESPN/CFBD data in a public
repository isn't appropriate.

## Validation

```{python}
done = g[g.completed & ~g.shortened]
mismatch = 0
for side in ("home", "away"):
    by_q = done[[f"{side}_q{i}" for i in range(1, 5)]].sum(axis=1) + done[f"{side}_ot"]
    mismatch += int((by_q != done[f"{side}_points"]).sum())
fbs = g[g.home_fbs & g.away_fbs]
fbs_teams = pd.concat([
    fbs[["season", "home_id"]].set_axis(["season", "team_id"], axis=1),
    fbs[["season", "away_id"]].set_axis(["season", "team_id"], axis=1),
]).drop_duplicates().groupby("season").size()
n_games, n_done = len(g), int(g.completed.sum())
n_short = int(g.shortened.sum())
```

Every check passes:

1. **One row per game.** `game_id` is unique across `{python} f"{n_games:,}"` games
   (`{python} f"{n_done:,}"` completed).
2. **Quarters add up.** Q1 + Q2 + Q3 + Q4 + OT equals the final score in every completed,
   full-length game (`{python} mismatch` mismatches).
3. **FBS membership is right.** A team counts as FBS in a season if it plays 6+ games in
   that season's FBS scoreboard; FCS opponents appear only in their one or two games
   against FBS teams. The counts match reality (128 teams in 2015, 134 in 2024).
4. **Weather-shortened games are flagged.** `{python} n_short` games ended before Q4
   (for example, Kentucky vs Southern Miss in 2024, called for lightning). They have no
   quarter or half targets and are excluded from training.

```{python}
#| label: fig-fbs-teams
#| fig-cap: "FBS teams per season, as identified from the scoreboard (2026 includes scheduled games)."
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6.5, 2.6))
ax.bar(fbs_teams.index, fbs_teams.values, color=BLUE, width=0.6)
ax.set_ylim(120, 142)
ax.set_ylabel("teams")
for x, v in zip(fbs_teams.index, fbs_teams.values):
    ax.text(x, v + 0.4, str(v), ha="center", fontsize=8, color=INK_2)
bar_ends(ax); plt.show()
```

## Coverage of lines and advanced stats

```{python}
#| label: tbl-coverage
#| tbl-cap: "Share of FBS-vs-FBS games with each data type, by season (%)."
f2 = g[g.completed & g.home_fbs & g.away_fbs & (g.season <= 2025)].merge(lines, on="game_id", how="left")
cov = pd.DataFrame({
    "games": f2.groupby("season").size(),
    "closing spread": f2.groupby("season").spread_close.apply(lambda s: 100 * s.notna().mean()),
    "opening spread": f2.groupby("season").spread_open.apply(lambda s: 100 * s.notna().mean()),
    "advanced stats": f2.assign(has=f2.game_id.isin(adv.game_id)).groupby("season").has.mean() * 100,
}).round(1)
cov
```

Two facts shape everything downstream:

- **Closing lines cover every game**, so the closing line is always available as the
  benchmark.
- **Opening lines only exist from 2021.** Anything trained *against the opener* has at
  most three seasons (2021–2023) before validation. That's why the market layer in
  @sec-modeling is deliberately tiny.

Consensus lines are the **median across books** (ESPN Bet, DraftKings, Bovada in recent
seasons).
